author: staurum
text:
wow... i just woke up to see some awesome discussions.

I do have something to show why the trade was inevitably left to be
taken, but to those who have dug deep into analysing why I took the
trade. please update/revise your analysis after these comments:

- try not only focus on entry's reason, but also try find symmetry of price dance floor I was looking for

- for me, subjectively, there was a PA foretelling the trade, which
looks like a touch trade without confirmation. this is very subjective,
but who knows someone can have the same thoughts.

- try to see bigger pictures, add the lines and look what has happened
in the past, this serves as a confluence. If you guys have done the
"Find the decisions" homeworks, you'll understand more, but if you
haven't, that homework is of paramount importance. this could easily
explain why I entried there.

- last thing: i am now trying NOT to think of set-ups or mechanical
thinking. always think about: MARKET = ROBBERY OF STOPS + ILLUSIONARY
TRAPS.

- just like IF said: "If there is no PA, there is trade" and "If the
trade is not begging to be taken, then no trade", or one more IF often
says something like "The stops are just begging to be taken".

- then, there was news anticipation, the evil ones won't make it easy, really.

Looking forward to your updated versions of analysis

If too long, then why not a video. hehe...

Just remember peeps,

when you're trying to emulate a master chef's recipe, it's natural to
measure out every ingredient to the milligram, and fuss about every
little detail.

But with tons of experience, there comes a time when you too become a
master chef, and what you do is shake in a bit of this and a bit of
that, knowing that what you're doing is right.

When it's time for you to write a cookbook of your own, you'll have to, for the reader, measure all the ingredients you put in.

and simple. Now, for the sake of the cookbook named Gold Digging,

Staurum, thanks for your explanation. When i ask about is this a
demand trading i was referred from a retailers perspective. So, what i
meant was that the retailers for sure would put their SL below 1 because
 they trade S/D only. So why would you put a SL for long just above the
retailers? Yes, you had buyers in,

but its so scary. If i would you, i dont know if i would trust such a
tight SL in these places . Maybe i'm wrong, Imagine you risk 5% and
price burst through your level.

I think a safe SL on this it could be at least below 1, and even that it
 wasn't deep enough. So, if price would broke your little level, as soon
 as it retrace back to your entry you could exit without loss.

However, you had a important thing on your side: the high was in very
higher TF in the middle, so there was nothing major from where price
came from.

author: staurum
text:
Sunday afternoon cookies & tea:

Again, i'm having a mind dumping exercise, while being grateful of all
the goods and the bads giving colour to our life. just like what Mark
Gungor said in:

we, boys, tend to go into our "nothing" box, just chill and think about
absolutely nothing. Well thinking about it, dat s not entirely true.
Even when someone is having a cup of coffee, or tea, or laying down on a
 sand sunbathing by the sea, or even smoking alone on a balcony; our
mind chatter, even without our slightest effort, just goes on and on
with incredibly many things revolving around our head as if there are
thousands of youtube videos or TV broadcasts roaming around making
noises all at the same time.

However, believe it or not, many if not most breakthrough ideas generate this way.

anyway, not wanting to brag too long, just a tip: when doing any
homework or analysis, try to voice-speak, i.e. talk to ourselves with
our own voice. Just thinking in mind or whispering inside head often
gets distracted. By listening to my own voice, I can sometimes develop
two or three personalities that debate one against another. It's very
very stupid, i know; so when i'm doing this, i can't let anyone near me,
 else become jokes.

but, to me, mostly something good comes out of it and makes my learning full of critiques and what-if scenarios.

Remember Rome is not built in a day and there are just too many ways to reach there?

Take a deep, long recovery rest for the battles ahead are long and hard,
 but we all have what we need here, don't stop believing.
